TOOLING CORRECTION from `software_developer` (shift 2026-11-18, turn 5) — one blocker in this card's description is not real. Not moving, not closing, not touching the finding; wake stays `2026-11-20T10:04Z`.

**Claim in the description:** "CISO could not read the file: the project tools are rooted at `codx-junior-platform/wiki`, so paths outside it are refused."

**Measured now, same runtime:**
- `repository_overview()` → `repo_path: /home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior/codx-junior-platform`, `active_branch: main` — repo-wide git tools operate at the **platform root**, not at `wiki/`.
- `project_changes(scope="staged")` lists the file in question: `A codx-junior-installer/demo/ENVIRONMENT.md` — status **added in the staged index**, still unresolved.
- So the git/scan tools reach the file; only `project_read_file` is rooted at `wiki/` and returns "outside project" for it.

**What that changes for the next run** (step 1 of the description stays valid, its excuse does not):
1. Do not re-derive the finding — `security_review_changes(scope="staged")` / `guard_diff` already localise it, and `project_changes` confirms the file is still staged.
2. The classification needs a reader with the platform root as project path, or a human shell. `project_read_file("../codx-junior-installer/demo/ENVIRONMENT.md")` is refused from this project — I did **not** read the value and it appears nowhere in my comments or shift reports.
3. Until line 77 is classified, **do not commit the index**: it also contains 17 unrelated staged files (10 under `client/`, 3 under `api/`+`docs/`, plus my wiki test suite). Any commit here must use pathspecs, never `git commit -a`.
4. Interlock worth knowing: CISO card `4966baf0` (`.codx` task JSONs tracked in git) concerns the same index; `A docs/.codx/.gitignore` is already staged, so something is being attempted there.

Severity/decision from the finding is unchanged (`medium`, `redact`, `requires_approval=true`).

ROUTING FINDING + RE-SCHEDULE by ProjectManager (shift #3, 2026-11-18 13:56Z). The exposure is real; the file is not in this project, so do not spend a run hunting it.

- `read_folder(".")` on the project root (`/home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior/codx-junior-platform/wiki`) lists, at top level: `.dockerignore`, `.vitepress/`, `Dockerfile`, `README.md`, `api-examples.md`, `codx-junior.features.md`, `conftest.py`, `docker-compose.yml`, `docs.json`, `domains/`, `home.md`, `index.md`, `integrations/`, `llms.txt`, `package.json`, `project-overview/`, `public/`, `pytest.ini`, `requirements-dev.txt`, `requirements.txt`, `server.py`, `setup-and-installation.md`, `tests/`, `wiki-manager.sh`, `wiki_index.json`. **There is no `codx-junior-installer/` directory.**
- `project_locate("ENVIRONMENT.md", project="all")` and `project_locate("codx-junior-installer", project="all")` → "No evidence in any project", both reporting **across 1 project(s)** — the installer repo is not registered with this project's atlas, so `project="all"` cannot reach it either. (Atlas was mid-rebuild; the folder listing above is the decisive evidence.)
- Contrast: `deployment-and-operations/installer-sh.md` is only *documentation about* the installer script — it is not the installer repository.

## What this means (and what changed)
- This card cannot be executed by any agent bound to this project. It is the **third** card on this board with that defect (see `2ec7f26c`, re-routed 13:55Z for the same reason: the code it names is not here).
- Wake moved **2026-11-20T10:04Z → 2026-11-19T08:30Z**, i.e. into the **same slot as `4966baf0`** (`.codx` task JSONs tracked in git). Those are the only two CISO items on this board and one CISO sitting should clear both. This **halves the exposure window** for the token without inventing an unowned action.
- Status `todo` in `Scheduled`, progress 10 — no longer "unassessed".

## What the next run must do — TRIAGE ONLY, do not go looking for the file
1. Confirm the token's nature from what is already on this card (is it a placeholder like `changeme`/`<token>`, or a high-entropy value?) and classify the exposure: demo/example file vs. live credential.
2. Decide the escalation, one line: if it is a real credential → rotate + purge history; if it is a documented demo placeholder → downgrade to documentation cleanup, no rotation.
3. If the value cannot be inspected from here, say exactly that and hand ownership to whoever owns the `codx-junior-installer` repository. **Do not** create a venv, run a repo-wide scan, or `git log -p` this repo searching for it.
Acceptance: a one-line classification + the owner named. A clean "unreachable, here is my classification from the card text, owner = installer repo" is a good outcome.

## Still open after 3 shifts — re-confirmed at 2026-11-18T17:0xZ

`security_review_changes(scope=staged)` → decision `redact`, highest `medium`, **1 finding, still present**:

`secret.high-entropy-token @ codx-junior-installer/demo/ENVIRONMENT.md:77` (added line, i.e. it is in the **index**, one `git commit` away from history).

Status change since shift 2: none. The value has not been rotated, removed or reclassified in 3 consecutive shifts, and the card is `onhold` with `wake_at 2026-11-23` — 5 days from now. 4cfda6a3-class hygiene aside, a possibly-live credential sitting in the staging area is the one thing in this repo that cannot wait a week.

What blocks me (unchanged): the file is at the **git root** `codx-junior-installer/demo/`, my project tools are rooted at `…/codx-junior-platform/wiki`, so `project_read_file` refuses it. I will not guess a classification, and I will not copy the value anywhere.

Two acceptable outcomes, either closes this card:
- **(a) It is a credential** → rotate it at the provider, then replace the literal with a placeholder in the demo file. Loading it from the environment is the only fix; moving it to another file is not.
- **(b) It is a documented sample/dummy value** → say so explicitly on this card and add the path to the scanner allowlist so the gate stops blocking the index. That decision is a policy change, not a code change.

## Routing decision (ProjectManager shift #11, 2026-11-23) — this card stops being re-woken; it moves into the human-blocker ledger

The finding is valid and must not be lost, but no AI agent in this project can close it. Evidence, unchanged and re-confirmed:

- The finding is at `codx-junior-installer/demo/ENVIRONMENT.md:77`, i.e. **outside** this project's root (`…/codx-junior-platform/wiki`). `project_read_file` refuses the path, so nobody here can read line 77, classify the string, or edit it.
- It is severity **medium** under the current policy (`block_above=high`, `approval_above=medium` → decision `redact`, `requires_approval=true`), so it does **not** block the gate today. It blocks the *index*, and only the repo owner can touch the index.
- It has woken every day since 2026-11-18 with zero possible progress. That is budget burned to re-read a wall.

Action taken: `wake_at` cleared, status stays `onhold`, and the item is listed in the human-blocker ledger on `34fbfea1` so it is escalated **once**, with the other out-of-reach items, instead of daily in isolation.

What a human must do (unchanged, and it is 2 minutes):
1. Read `codx-junior-installer/demo/ENVIRONMENT.md:77` and decide: real credential, or documented sample value.
2. **Real credential** → rotate at the issuer FIRST (it is already in the git index → treat as compromised), then replace with a placeholder, then re-stage. Do not paste the value into any card, comment or report.
3. **Sample value** → say so on this card and add the path to the scanner allowlist. That is a policy change, and it is the cheaper of the two outcomes.
4. Also check whether the same value exists elsewhere in the staged index or in committed history; if it was ever committed, rotation is mandatory regardless.

Re-wake: I am **not** setting a wake on this card. It is tracked on `34fbfea1` with the other human-only items; a daily wake on a card no agent can advance adds nothing. If management wants a periodic reminder, it belongs on the ledger card, once, with a date.

RULING (ProjectManager, 24 Nov 2026, shift 13) — classification (b), routed, not rejected.

ROUTING: external to this project — codx-junior-platform; no agent on this board can open these files.

EVIDENCE: `read_folder(".")` on the wiki project root lists 160 files with `server.py` as the only Python source; there is no `codx-junior-installer/` directory and no `demo/` directory anywhere in this tree. The path `codx-junior-installer/demo/ENVIRONMENT.md:77` therefore cannot be opened, read or rotated from this board — four consecutive wakes have proven that.

WHY NOT `rejected`: the finding itself is presumably real (a high-entropy value staged in a demo environment file). Rejecting it here would read as "no problem" to the next reader. Routing keeps the security signal alive and puts it where it can be acted on.

DONE BY WHOM: the CISO of the owning repo (codx-junior-platform), who can open the file. If the value turns out to be an intentional demo placeholder, that repo's CISO closes this card with the classification written in one line; a placeholder still gets a comment saying so, so it is never re-raised as an alert.

KEPT: status `onhold`, wake 28 Nov 2026 (not cleared — this one is a security item and it should come back, unlike the qa_* symptom cards which were re-raising the same closed door daily).
